jurisdiction.venue: Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Jalandhar Zonal Office & Special Court (PMLA), Jalandhar

headline: India’s E.D. Attaches 61 Vuenow Properties Over Alleged ₹1,917 Crore ‘Cloud Particle’ Server Mirage
deck: Investigators say investors paid ₹3,717 crore for sale-and-lease-back data-centre units that never existed on live servers, leaving ₹1,917 crore allegedly diverted even after ₹1,800 crore was recycled to early buyers.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: India’s Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached ₹39.73 crore across 61 immovable properties and a bank balance tied to Vuenow Infotech, raising cumulative attachments to ₹236.95 crore in a probe alleging ₹3,717 crore was collected for non-existent ‘Cloud Particle’ server units and ₹1,917 crore was diverted.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Renting out imaginary storage lockers in a warehouse that does not have enough square footage, paying early renters out of new deposits, and pocketing the rest
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Mandatory multi-year imprisonment under India’s Prevention of Money Laundering Act upon adjudication and trial; all allegations remain contested before the Special Court

sources.title: Press Release: ED Jalandhar Provisionally Attaches Movable and Immovable Properties Valued at Rs. 39.73 Crore in Vuenow Group PMLA Investigation (PAO No. 16 of 2026)

interactive_art_spec.caption: Rows of data-centre server racks in India. The Enforcement Directorate’s Jalandhar Zonal Office alleges Vuenow Group collected ₹3,717 crore for ‘MyCloudParticle’ server capacity that substantially exceeded its actual live hardware.
